message: I'll replace slide 3 with three slides: slide 3 becomes an overview of the four patterns, and new slides 4 and 5 cover system prompts with few-shot examples, and chain-of-thought with structured output. The impact, workflow and checklist slides become slides 6 to 8.

slides.purpose: Introduce the core techniques: an overview of the four prompt design patterns
slides.content_brief: Overview slide naming the four key patterns — system-prompt framing, few-shot examples, chain-of-thought reasoning, and structured output formatting — as four labelled tiles, with a one-line note that the next two slides cover them in pairs
slides.assumes: Audience understands the problem from the previous slide
slides.hands_off: Four composable patterns cover the vast majority of prompt optimisation needs

slides.purpose: Explain the first two patterns: system-prompt framing and few-shot examples
slides.content_brief: Two-column slide with system-prompt framing (set the role, constraints and tone once) on the left and few-shot examples (show two or three input-output pairs) on the right, each with a one-line example and when to use it
slides.assumes: Audience has just seen the four patterns named
slides.hands_off: Framing and examples show the model what a good answer looks like

slides.purpose: Explain the other two patterns: chain-of-thought reasoning and structured output
slides.content_brief: Two-column slide with chain-of-thought reasoning (ask for the steps before the answer) on the left and structured output formatting (a schema or template for the reply) on the right, each with a one-line example and when to use it, and a callout on when to combine the patterns
slides.assumes: Audience knows system-prompt framing and few-shot examples from the last slide
slides.hands_off: Reasoning steps and a fixed output shape make answers reliable and checkable
